sections.html:
Salisbury is the county seat of Wicomico County and the largest city on Maryland's Eastern Shore, about 106 miles from Baltimore and 119 miles from Washington. The population was 30,343 in 2010 and 33,050 in 2020. Poultry, health care, education and distribution drive the local economy.

Three historic areas are protected by the city: Camden, Newtown and Downtown. Houses there need a separate review for exterior changes. Water is the main worry for owners, since the city sits only 17 to 45 feet above sea level at the head of the Wicomico River. If your house has roof or tree damage from a past storm, say so when you describe it.

A Salisbury homeowner receives one bill from Wicomico County and another from the City of Salisbury. The city began billing its own taxes with fiscal year 2019 to 2020, after the county ended its contract to process the city's bills.

For fiscal 2026 the county real property rate is 0.8099 and the city rate is 1.0332, a combined 1.8431 inside the city.

Property just outside the city but in the county carries only the county rate.

  • Wicomico County taxes are collected by the Wicomico Department of Finance at 125 N. Division Street, Salisbury.
  • For city taxes, call the City Finance Department at 410-548-3110.
  • Wicomico County does not currently impose a county transfer tax, though state law allows up to 1%.

Maryland reassesses each property every three years and phases the increase in equally over three years. An appeal of a new assessment must be filed within 45 days of the notice date with the local assessment office. Do not wait on this if you are about to list, since the assessment affects the tax split at closing.

Salisbury asks the owner to sign a Property Affidavit, sworn before a notary, and file it with the city's Internal Services Office before the deed is stamped.

  • The owner acknowledges city codes, including the property maintenance, plumbing and building codes.
  • The owner states the proposed use: owner-occupied, rental, commercial, a care or recovery-type residence, or other.
  • If the property will be rented, the owner must register the unit and get a rental license within 60 days of ownership or of it becoming a rental. The affidavit lists a $500 fine for failing to comply.
  • For homes in the Camden, Newtown or Downtown historic districts, exterior changes need a certificate of approval from the Salisbury Historic District Commission.

The buyer's side usually handles this form, but know it exists so the closing does not stall.

sections.h2: Rental owner license and vacant building fees
sections.html:
Salisbury requires a Rental Owner's License before any unit is registered. Renewals are due March 1 each year through the city's OpenGov portal.

Fee typeFirst yearRenewal
Rental owner's license$120$75
Each rental unit registered$120$75
Vacant residential building registration$200 a year$100 inspection after year one
  • New units must pass inspection before a license is issued, and failed units get a Corrective Action Letter.
  • A reinspection costs $100 if required.
  • Each business entity, such as an LLC, needs its own license and registrations.
  • Pre-1978 properties need a lead certificate uploaded at renewal and for new tenants.

Code citations range from $25 to $500 per day depending on the violation, and unpaid fines or abatement costs can become a lien on the property. A vacant, unregistered or unlicensed rental can carry these costs without the owner realizing it, so check the city record before you price a sale.

sections.h2: Selling a rental, inherited or repair-heavy house
sections.html:
Rental houses, inherited houses and houses with deferred repairs run into the licensing and code steps above, and a listing can stall while the owner sorts them out.

A cash buyer can purchase the property as it is, but the legal steps remain: the affidavit, a clean title and any rental registration the city requires. A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting. Ask for a written offer, read the closing terms, and have your own settlement company confirm each item before you sign.

U.S. 13 runs north and south toward Dover and Norfolk, and U.S. 50 runs east and west toward Ocean City and the Baltimore and Washington region. The Salisbury Bypass routes both around the city. Wicomico Regional Airport has daily American Eagle service to Philadelphia and Charlotte, and Shore Transit runs local buses.

Salisbury gets about 47.49 inches of precipitation and about 8.0 inches of snow a year. Fire and flood shaped the old downtown: blazes in 1860 and 1886 burned about two-thirds of the town, and the Humphreys Dam burst in 1909 and flooded parts of the city. A tornado rated EF1 struck on August 7, 2017.

sections.h2: Closing day and what a cash sale skips
sections.html:
At settlement the title company collects the signed deed, pays the county and city tax balances and any liens from your proceeds, and sends you the rest. Bring photo ID and keys. Read the settlement statement before signing and compare each tax line with your latest bills from the county and the city.

A cash buyer has no lender, so there is no appraisal to fail and no loan approval to wait on. For a Salisbury house with a rental history or an open code citation, that can mean a firm closing date, provided the city items are cleared first. Ask the city for a written statement of what is open on the address, and keep it with your closing papers.

• The latest tax bills from both the county and the city.
  • Your rental license and unit registration, if the house was leased.
  • Any Corrective Action Letter or code citation, with proof the work was done.
  • The vacant building registration, if the house has stood empty.
  • The lead certificate, for a pre-1978 rental.

Sellers who collect these before talking to buyers get cleaner offers, and the title company spends less time chasing the city for answers.

1. Pull the city record for open code citations, vacancy registration and rental licenses.
  2. Request both tax balances, one from the county and one from the city.
  3. Make sure the Property Affidavit is filed before the deed is stamped.
  4. Complete the Maryland disclosure or disclaimer form.
  5. Close, with the settlement company paying taxes and liens from your proceeds.

If you own the house through an LLC, remember that the entity needs its own license and registrations.

faqs.q: Is Salisbury, MD the county seat of Wicomico County?
faqs.a: Yes. Salisbury became the seat when Wicomico County was formed in 1867. It is the largest city on Maryland's Eastern Shore.

faqs.q: Does Salisbury bill its own property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Starting with fiscal year 2019 to 2020, owners get one bill from the City of Salisbury and a separate one from Wicomico County. The fiscal 2026 city and county real property rates are 1.0332 and 0.8099.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell a rented house in Salisbury?
faqs.a: A rental owner must hold a license and register each unit, and a buyer who keeps the house as a rental must do the same within 60 days of ownership. Ask the city whether your current registration is in good standing before you sell.

faqs.q: What is the Salisbury Property Affidavit?
faqs.a: It is a sworn form the owner files with the city's Internal Services Office before the deed is stamped. It confirms the proposed use of the property and acknowledges city codes, rental registration and historic district rules.

faqs.q: What can Salisbury fine for code violations?
faqs.a: City code citations range from $25 to $500 per day depending on the violation. Unpaid fines or abatement costs can become a lien on the property.
